original_record.reason: Ready. Complete recorded proof strategy (M17). Well-definedness: h extended by zero to N is smooth since supp h is compact in the open U, so A+sh is smooth on N for every real s; L(A), ell_1, ell_2 are continuous on the compact closure of the bounded U and U has finite Lebesgue measure, so all integrals below are finite. Expansion: F(s)=F+sG by derivative linearity; bilinearity of eta and antisymmetry F^{mu nu}=-F^{nu mu} give F^{mu nu}G_{mu nu}=2F^{mu nu}partial_mu h_nu, hence L(A+sh)=L(A)+s*ell_1+s^2*ell_2 and the derivative integral in (a). Conversion: F^{mu nu} is C^1, so its classical partial derivative is its weak derivative (lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives, AC_omega) and the weak test identity gives integral F^{mu nu}partial_mu h_nu = -integral (partial_mu F^{mu nu})h_nu with no boundary term because h is compactly supported in U; this is (b). Coefficient equation (c): the continuous g_nu=kappa^{-1}partial_mu F^{mu nu}+J^nu vanishes by the vector clause of lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma, and the converse is immediate. Re-recorded after restoring def-euclidean-inner-product, which supplies the inner-product notation under which the first variation is written as the pairing of g with h in the strategy. Only constancy/symmetry/nondegeneracy of eta are used, and the recorded statement is the design's M17 claim with its disclaimers (no existence of stationary fields; physical readings are later choices). All 12 deps read; def-em-minkowski-affine-space is an in-run batch-14 supplier with a cross-batch row; AC_omega declared and used only through the two choice-dependent suppliers.

original_record.reason: Ready. Complete explicit mathematical example with two exact checks; re-recorded because both transitive A-item dependencies changed (inner-product supplier restored, one inaccurate cross-reference removed); the example's own statement and deps are unchanged. (i) On R^2, S(x,y)=x^2-y^2 has vanishing differential at the origin while S(eps,0)=eps^2 and S(0,eps)=-eps^2, so stationarity is a first-order condition with no minimality or existence content: it bounds what lem-em-compact-field-variation and lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma assert, at the level of explicit finite-dimensional calculus. (ii) With U=(-1,1)^4, kappa=1, J=0, A_0=(x^1)^2: F_01=-2x^1, F^{01}=2x^1, partial_1 F^{10}=-2 so the coefficient equation fails at nu=0, yet along the smooth non-compactly-supported variation h_0=1 the integrand L=2(x^1)^2 is independent of s and the first variation vanishes; hence the compact-support hypothesis of the compact-field lemma is essential to its integration-by-parts conversion (b) and stationarity equivalence (c). Deps read: both A items (statements and recorded strategies) and the index conventions of def-em-minkowski-affine-space; all steps exact algebra with no physical assumption or empirical claim. sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10, 246 PDF pages (author-published undergraduate textbook; signature (+---) converted to (-+++))
sources.locator: Section 1.3 'Measurement' pp. 23-27 (1.3.1 Invariants, 1.3.2 The metric, 1.3.3 The gamma factor), Section 1.4 'The Lorentz transformation' pp. 30-31, and Chapter 2 'Foundations (optional)' sections 2.1-2.5 pp. 43-51; the reader ledger records all ten chapters read, and the load-bearing sections above were read in the extracted text

contents.name: Section 1.3.1 'Invariants': light-rectangle area, gliding-clock proper time, and the area-based derivation of the interval t^2 - x^2
contents.reason: The area-based operational derivation of the invariant interval is motivational context; the formulated framework adopts the Lorentz form, orientation, time orientation and clock interpretation as primitives rather than deriving them from area and symmetry postulates.

contents.name: Section 1.3.2 'The metric': g(u,v) = u_t v_t - u_x v_x - u_y v_y - u_z v_z, signature (+---), and the SI/natural-unit variants of Example 5
contents.support: The metric is absorbed into the model definition with the stated conversion from signature (+---) to (-+++) and with x^0 = ct fixed by the unit conventions of this page.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 'The gamma factor': time dilation, the gamma factor 1/sqrt(1-v^2), and Examples 7-10 (Pioneer 10, atomic clocks, muons)
contents.reason: Time dilation and the gamma factor are statements about clocks carried along worldlines; they belong to the clock/proper-time development, and the empirical examples are secondary narrative, not primary-report data.

contents.name: Section 1.3.4 and the interstellar road-trip Example 8: length contraction
contents.reason: Length measurement presupposes simultaneity and radar protocols; the observer-measurements page defines those and proves the length transformation, so the material is not repeated among the primitives.

contents.name: Section 1.4 'The Lorentz transformation': equation (1) t' = gamma(t - vx), x' = -v gamma t + gamma x, the light-speed-line and determinant-one checks, and Examples 11-12
contents.reason: The transformation formulas, their inverse and composition, and the invariance of the interval and cones are the subject of the next SR page, which proves them from the affine model built here.

contents.name: Section 2.1 'Causality': the arrow of time, initial-value problems, and the modest causality postulate P1
contents.reason: These are foundational discussions about how to axiomatize causality; this formulation adopts the affine model with a chosen time orientation directly and retains no deduction of P1 from a physical arrow-of-time principle.

contents.name: Section 2.2 'Flatness': failure of parallelism, parallel transport, the flatness postulate P2, and the Gravity Probe B discussion
contents.reason: Path-dependence of parallel transport is a curvature statement belonging to the general-relativity material; the special-relativity framework adopts the flat affine model without deriving flatness from transport experiments.

contents.name: Section 2.3 'Additional postulates' P3-P6 and Section 2.4 'Other axiomatizations' (Einstein's E1-E2, the T-system, and the comparison of P/E/T)
contents.reason: Reconstruction of the affine Lorentz framework from the verbal symmetry postulates is reserved to the Lorentz-transformations page's remark on the reconstruction obligations; the primitives page adopts the geometry outright.

contents.name: Section 2.5: spacetime area is a relativistic invariant, and Chapter 2 Problems 1-5

contents.name: Section 1.4 remark: the Lorentz transformation is not reducible to length contraction and time dilation, and 1+1 dimensions are used only for convenience
contents.reason: This is a caution against an erroneous reduction; the library represents the transformation by its exact algebraic statements and worked examples, and no separate formal claim exists to scaffold.

contents.name: Sections 2.3-2.4: the symmetry postulates P3 (homogeneity and isotropy), P4 (existence of inertial frames), P5 (equivalence of uniformly moving frames), P6 (relativity of time), and Einstein's E1-E2 together with the T1-T2 maximal-proper-time system
contents.support: The remark records which formal assumptions those verbal systems contain and lists the reconstruction obligations (homogeneity/isotropy, inertial-frame existence, operational simultaneity, affine group preserving a quadratic form, global topology) that this framework does not discharge.

contents.name: Section 2.4.3: the claim that the P, E and T axiomatizations are logically equivalent, and the comparison with doubly-special relativity
contents.reason: The claimed equivalence of the verbal axiom systems is neither re-proved nor used here; the remark treats reconstruction from them as an open obligation, so there is no scaffolded claim to attach this source-level assertion to.

contents.name: Section 2.2.3: the flatness postulate P2, the Gravity Probe B precession narrative and the small-region qualification of flatness
contents.reason: Flatness of the adopted model is a primitive assumption of this framework, and curvature tests belong to the general-relativity content; no special-relativity item is derived from this narrative here.

contents.name: Section 2.5: proof that spacetime area in the x-t plane is invariant from the postulates P1-P6 via the lattice construction

contents.name: Section 8.3.2 'Boosts': the numerical example in which a boost along x followed by a boost along y differs from the reversed order, with the discrepancy a rotation of order v^2

contents.name: Section 8.3.1 'Rotations': rotations about different axes do not commute, with the numerical discrepancy of order theta^2

contents.support: The definition states the same metric-preservation condition on the abstract Lorentz vector space and records the matrix criterion M^T eta_0 M = eta_0 in an eta-orthonormal basis, with the group structure proved in a separate lemma.

contents.support: The lemma proves beta = tanh r, gamma = cosh r and the displayed hyperbolic matrix from the exponential definitions, and derives the composition law from the addition formula.

contents.name: Paragraphs after (1.14): rotations, boosts and discrete time/space reversals; the proper Lorentz group SO(3,1) as the exclusion of the reversals; non-commutativity of the general six-parameter group; and the Poincare group of translations and Lorentz transformations
contents.support: The counterexample supplies the exact matrices Pi and T, their determinants and their orthochrony classes, witnessing that excluding the discrete transformations is a genuine restriction and that det = 1 alone is not enough.

contents.name: Paragraph after (1.14), continued: the Poincare group as the ten-parameter group of translations and Lorentz transformations
contents.support: The affine Lorentz maps of the definition are exactly the compositions of a translation with a linear Lorentz map, which is the source's Poincare group without its spinorial generalisation.

contents.name: Light-cone discussion (p. 7): the set of light-speed trajectories x = +-t is invariant under Lorentz transformations, light cones are naturally divided into future and past, and timelike/spacelike/null separation

contents.name: Spacetime diagram paragraph: under a boost the x'-axis is t = x tanh phi and the t'-axis is t = x/tanh phi, and the axes scissor together instead of remaining Euclidean-orthogonal

contents.name: Section 3.5.1 'The velocity vector': v = dr/dtau as the derivative of the world-line by proper time, and the explicit statement that a velocity vector is only defined for particles whose world-lines are timelike (a ray of light has dtau = 0 and dr/dtau has infinite components)
contents.support: The definition U = x'/tau' with tau' > 0 encodes exactly this restriction: the four-velocity is introduced for future timelike worldlines, and the null case is excluded because tau is not strictly increasing there.

contents.name: Section 3.5.1: the light-ray case Delta tau = 0, so that dr/dtau is not a vector defined on null world-lines
contents.support: The counterexample is the exact algebraic form of this observation for the null line k = (1,1,0,0): the integrand vanishes identically, there is no proper-time parameter and no normalized timelike four-velocity.

contents.name: Section 3.5.2 'The acceleration vector': a = dv/dtau, the curvature of the world-line, and the identification of minus a.a with the square of the proper acceleration read by a comoving accelerometer (source signature (+---))
contents.support: The item defines A = U'/tau' in the (-+++) convention; the proper-acceleration magnitude is derived from eta(A,A) in clause (e) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition and computed for circular motion on the companion page.

contents.name: Example 3 'Velocity vector of an object at rest': v = (1,0) and dt/dtau = 1
contents.support: The example is the c-retained, (-+++) form of the same statement: x(t) = (ct,a_1,a_2,a_3) has U = (c,0,0,0), u = e_0 and tau(t) - tau(t_0) = t - t_0.

contents.name: Example 4 'Constant proper acceleration': t = (1/a) sinh(a tau), x = (1/a) cosh(a tau), the hyperbolic world-line, its lightlike asymptote and the associated event horizon
contents.reason: The hyperbolic world-line, its asymptote and the accelerated-observer horizon are the explicit calculation and chart-domain subject of the accelerated-observers page, whose design reserves proper acceleration, Rindler charts and the horizon discussion; nothing in this pair uses them.

contents.name: Section 3.5.3 'Counting degrees of freedom': the eight components of the velocity and acceleration vectors carry two hidden constraints
contents.support: The two constraints are exactly eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0, proved as clauses (a) and (b); the counting argument itself is the source's motivation, not a separate claim to scaffold.

contents.name: Section 3.5.3 'Normalization of the velocity': v.v = 1 always, so the velocity vector is the tangent vector that is future-directed and normalized to unit length
contents.support: Clause (a) proves eta(U,U) = -c^2, i.e. v.v = 1 in the source's c = 1, (+---) convention; clause (c) records the rest-space geometry that the geometric reading of the definition uses.

contents.name: Section 3.5.3 'Orthogonality of the velocity and acceleration': a.v = 0 for every possible velocity and acceleration pair
contents.support: Clause (b) proves eta(U,A) = 0 by differentiating the norm identity, which is the coordinate-free form of a.v = 0.

contents.name: Section 3.5.3 'self-check C': whether a vector that qualifies as a valid velocity vector in one frame can be invalid in another
contents.support: The answer is the Lorentz invariance of eta and of future timelikeness (the batch-2 lemma lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure), used here through the norm identity; the self-check is a question, not a separate named result.

contents.name: Section 3.6 'Some kinematic identities': D(v) = sqrt((1+v)/(1-v)), gamma = (D + D^{-1})/2, v = tanh eta, gamma = cosh eta, v gamma = sinh eta, D_c = D_1 D_2 and eta_c = eta_1 + eta_2 for collinear boosts
contents.support: These are the rapidity identities of collinear boosts, proved on the Lorentz-transformations page (batch 2); this pair uses none of them, so they are absorbed there rather than re-minted.

contents.name: Section 3.6: definitions of sinh, cosh, tanh, their inverse formulas sinh^{-1} x = ln(x + sqrt(x^2+1)), cosh^{-1}, tanh^{-1} = (1/2) ln((1+x)/(1-x)), and the derivative formulas (x^2+1)^{-1/2}, (x^2-1)^{-1/2}, (1-x^2)^{-1}
contents.reason: These derivative formulas are used by the constant-proper-acceleration and Rindler calculations of the accelerated-observers page; this pair uses only the elementary power, product and chain rules of the imported real-analysis items.

contents.name: Section 3.7 'The projection operator': P_o r = r - (r.o)/(o.o) o, with properties 1-8 (o.P_o r = 0, r - P_o r parallel to o, P_o o = 0, idempotence, linearity, derivative commutation, and the split v = P_o v + gamma o)
contents.support: Clause (c) is the same projection written with a normalized observer, h(v) = v + eta(n,v) n; the identities h(n) = 0, h o h = h, eta(n,h(v)) = 0 and the unique decomposition are exactly the source's properties 3, 4, 1 and 2.

contents.name: Section 3.7: the conversion table between four-vectors and observer three-vectors, v_o = P_o v/(o.v), v = gamma (o + v_o), a_o = (1/(o.v)^2)[P_o a - (o.a) v_o] and a = gamma^3 (a_o.v_o) v + gamma^2 a_o
contents.support: With a normalized observer n = e_0 in an inertial chart the table becomes the coordinate clause (e): U = gamma_w (c,w) and the displayed components of A; the general-observer split is clause (d).

contents.name: Section 3.7: the identity d gamma/dt = gamma^3 a_o.v_o used in differentiating the transformation of four-vectors
contents.support: The same identity in the form d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 is the differentiation step of clause (e), where gamma_w is the Lorentz factor of the coordinate velocity.

contents.name: Example 5 'Lewis-Tolman paradox': rotational equilibrium of a system of particles and the transformation of its accelerations
contents.reason: The paradox concerns angular momentum and the equilibrium of an extended rotating system, for which this framework has no model on this page; the acceleration transformation it illustrates is already available as coordinate clause (e), so no separate item is warranted.

contents.name: Section 4, Theorem 1: Fundamental Lemma of the Calculus of Variations (one-variable statement; proof by contradiction with a bump supported where f > c > 0 and f h > c h)
contents.support: The recorded scalar proof follows exactly this contradiction pattern: a point where g > 0, a ball on which g >= g(p)/2, a nonnegative bump supported in that ball, and the positivity of the resulting pairing. The pair replaces the source's explicit bump construction with the published cutoff lemma lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization and closes the positivity step through the localization lemma and the order rules for the nonnegative integral.

contents.name: Section 4, construction of the smooth bump phi_{a,b}(t) = theta((t-a)/(b-a)) theta((b-t)/(b-a)) with theta(t) = e^{-1/t}, its positivity, and Remark 1 that it suffices to test smooth h
contents.support: Confirms that the test family in the pair's hypothesis can be taken smooth (C_c^infinity) and that the bump construction yields properties (P1) and (P2), the integral positivity pattern the recorded proof consumes.

contents.name: Section 14, Theorem 4: multidimensional version of the Fundamental Lemma (continuous f on a bounded open D, C^2 test functions vanishing on the boundary, product-of-bumps inside a hypercube) and Exercise 19

contents.name: Section 14, classical fields: variation of the functional I[phi] = integral of L, the boundary flux integral over dR, the two admissible variation choices (fast decay or compact support), and the Euler-Lagrange equation (9) via the Fundamental Lemma, with the remark that the h of Theorem 4 has compact support

The pair's item instantiates this for the kappa-scaled quadratic functional -F_{mu nu}F^{mu nu}/(4 kappa) + J^nu A_nu on a bounded open subset of R^4 with the (-,+,+,+) Minkowski conventions of def-em-minkowski-affine-space, and records the compact-support test identity explicitly instead of discarding a total derivative.

coverage.note: Convention dictionary. Tong uses the (+,-,-,-) Minkowski metric and couples the source with -A_mu J^mu, obtaining partial_mu F^{mu nu} = mu_0 J^nu; this pair uses the (-,+,+,+) form eta of def-em-minkowski-affine-space and the density -F_{mu nu}F^{mu nu}/(4 kappa) + J^nu A_nu, obtaining partial_mu F^{mu nu} = -kappa J^nu. Only the computation's structure is reused, and every sign is rederived in the pair's conventions. Figueroa-O'Farrill's Theorem 4 states the multidimensional fundamental lemma for C^2 functions vanishing on the boundary of a bounded open set; the pair states the C_c^infinity(U) form, whose bump construction and compact support are the source's, with smoothness delegated to the published cutoff lemma. Particle-curve variation (V1) and gauge/source compatibility (V2) belong to em-expanded-analysis-prerequisites and em-action-and-variational-formulation respectively and are not built on this pair.
